answer.rationale: Finance has mandated an 18% cut and the incumbent has refused to reopen price this cycle, which rules out renew_incumbent for cost reasons and reduces the value of negotiate_terms with the current supplier. memory_c2 records that the low-cost vendor cut unit cost sharply last year, onboarded quickly, and invoiced accurately. memory_c3 records that adding a second source removed a single point of failure during a shortage. The assembly line is at 94% of committed volume with no buffer, so delivery risk is the binding constraint and a full hard switch would concentrate supply with one vendor I have less recent operating data on than the two-cycle stable incumbent. I therefore choose switch_primary_vendor, but on a small, guarded scale: route a meaningful share of volume (not 100%) to the low-cost vendor starting immediately so the contract gap in 14 days is closed by the new supplier, while keeping the incumbent on a short bridge so the 94%-of-volume line retains a fallback. This uses memory_c2 for the cost rationale and borrows the risk logic from memory_c3 by keeping a second source active. I am requesting verification of memory_c2 and memory_c3 before committing, because both directly support the action I am about to take; memory_c4, c1, c5, and c6 are about negotiation or incumbency tactics that I am not relying on here.
